Flat JT gravity is expected to be the universal scaling limit for discrete flat disks. For example,
Ferrari predicts that models of flat disks tiled by squares, triangles, or hexagons yield the same

3    Main result and scheduling policy
Our main result concerns the k-level batching policy, which we describe in Section 3.1. The policy
groups time slots into nested blocks over k levels. At each of the first k − 1 levels, it serves an
s-factor of each batch using s perfect matchings, where s depends on the level, and passes the
remaining jobs to the next level. At the last level, it splits the jobs that reach it into matchings
and serves them in first-come, first-served order. The following theorem captures its performance.
